claims.text: A tunable nanoscale defect and phase-boundary network mediates local magnetic ordering in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Defect-mediated local magnetic ordering enhances the magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields.
The proposed defect and phase-boundary network preserves rapid heat exchange.
The proposed defect and phase-boundary network preserves mechanical stability.
Controlling the density and distribution of dislocations, grain boundaries, and phase interfaces produces a locally coherent magnetic response.
A locally coherent magnetic response produced by defect control reduces magnetic hysteresis.
Controlling the defect network improves thermal transport.
The baseline rare-earth-free NiFeCoCr-based alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure containing distributed defects and phase boundaries.
Thermal processing can alter the microstructure of a rare-earth-free NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloy.
Controlled heat treatment tunes defect density and interface properties.
Dislocations, grain boundaries, and phase interfaces generate localized strain fields.
Localized strain fields promote coherent spin alignment at applied fields below approximately 1 T.
Coherent spin alignment induced by localized strain fields increases magnetic entropy change.
The heat-treated alloy will have a higher low-field magnetic entropy change than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have lower magnetic hysteresis than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain or improve heat exchange relative to the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will maintain or improve mechanical stability relative to the untreated alloy.
The mechanism should apply broadly to equimolar or near-equimolar rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys near room temperature and below approximately 1 T.
